text:
Maya: FYI — kv-cache alerts spiked again 03:40 UTC, noisy pages to oncall. Postmortem created: https://redwood.company/pm/kv-cache-2026-03-01 :link:
Dan: Saw it. Looks like the dedupe window isn't catching the burst pattern. pager hit 4x within 12m.
Kevin: Can you paste the alert rule? might be threshold + eval_period both too low.
Maya: Here’s the rule block we used:
```
alert: kvcache_high_errors
expr: sum(rate(kv_cache_errors_total[1m])) by (shard) > 50
for: 1m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://runbooks/redwood/kvcache
```
Sophia: Two quick thoughts: 1) bump eval window to 5m 2) add dedupe by "deployment" or "service_shard" tag rather than shard alone
Nate: Also consider adding a sliding suppression: if same stacktrace/metric fires >3 times in 6m, create a single page and escalate only on sustained increase.
Tara: I can own the rule change and can push a canary patch to staging today. ETA 2h.
Maya: Thanks @Tara. Can you also add a dashboard graph for per-shard 5m rate and a sample time range overlay for last 7 days?
Tara: Yep. Will add dashboard + rule change. Will post PR link here.
Dan: Ownership: Tara for implementation, Kevin for review, Maya for post-deploy validation. Timeline: PR today, staging test tonight, prod roll tomorrow morning (unless staging fails).
Kevin: I'll review PR within 3h. If we need to change severity label from "page" -> "ticket" for lower-confidence bursts, let's do that in staging.
Sophia: Quick reminder: we have a recurring incident pattern with kv-cache every 3-4 weeks after deploys. Should we add a deploy-hook that runs a smoke check against cache miss rates? If so, who's on that?
Maya: Good call. Nate and I can draft a smoke test. Target for initial smoke check: next sprint (2 weeks).
Nate: I'll put a ticket in the ops backlog and tag as P2. Link when created.
IncidentBot: alert escalations: kvcache_high_errors triggered 2026-03-01T03:40:12Z -> 4 pages, resolved 03:53:21Z, incident link: https://incidents/redwood/9876
Tara: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/infra-alerts/pulls/452 — implements for:5m and dedupe labels + suppression logic. PTAL @Kevin @Maya
Kevin: Reviewing now. Minor nit on the label name, but LGTM otherwise.
Maya: Post-deploy checklist:
- [ ] Merge PR
- [ ] Monitor staging 6h for regressions
- [ ] Rollout to prod (gradual 10/30/60)
- [ ] Run smoke tests on next deploy
Dan: Also add a metric to track "pages avoided by dedupe" so we can quantify noise reduction over next month.
Sophia: For paging policy: proposal
- if alerts fire but resolved within 10m -> no page (pager -> ticket)
- sustained >10m -> page
- high-severity true positives still page immediately
We should document exceptions in the runbook.
Maya: Action items summary (assignments & ETA):
- Tara: PR and dashboard (today, done by EOD) — assigned
- Kevin: PR review (today, 3h) — assigned
- Maya: Post-deploy validation and runbook update (tomorrow morning) — assigned
- Nate: Create ops ticket for deploy smoke tests (this afternoon) — assigned
- Dan: Add telemetry metric for dedupe impact (next week) — assigned
- Sophia: Draft paging policy wording & exceptions (next week) — assigned
Tara: Updated PR to include severity toggle and added test cases. CI green.
Kevin: Merged, rolling to staging now.
Maya: Staging looks clean after 90m. No extra pages in that window. Rolling to prod per 10/30/60.
Dan: Prod rollout started 08:10 UTC. Monitoring.
Tara: Prod reached 60% at 08:22, no pages fired. Continuing.
Maya: Prod at 100% 08:35, no new pages. Will keep the dedupe metric dashboard and report back in 7 days.
Nate: Ops ticket: https://issues.redwood/ops/3223 — smoke test story added, ETA sprint-end.
Sophia: thanks everyone. Follow-up retro in next oncall meeting to see if noise dropped. :thumbsup:
Maya: Closing loop — will update postmortem with assigned owners and timeline. If anything else crops up ping #eng-oncall. :white_check_mark:
